dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, hi. Um, I'm calling about the snow plow. The plow went by and it buried the end of my driveway. Like a wall of snow, it's just sitting right across the whole opening.
Okay, so the plow came down your street and left a pile at the end of the driveway. Is that right?

Yes, exactly. And it's not like a little pile. It's packed, it's heavy, it's about up to my knees. I tried with a shovel for a bit and it's like shoveling a, a sidewalk. Sorry, you can hear me okay? I'm on speaker.
I can hear you fine. Go ahead. When did the plow come through?
So it was, um, this morning. Early. I heard it around, I want to say six? Maybe quarter of seven. Because I was up and then I went back to bed, and then I got up and looked out and, yeah. Wall.
Alright, this morning, early. And is the street itself cleared, or is it still covered?

The street's clear. It's plowed all the way, that's the thing. It's just the end of my driveway that got the pile. [pause] Wait, what was I going to say. Oh, I just want to ask if somebody can come back and, you know, plow it out. Or clear it. Whatever the right word is.
Sure. So you're asking for a plow to come back to your street and clear that pile at the end of the driveway.
Yes. Please. A plow coming back, that's it.
Okay. I'll need your address so I can put this in for the crew. What's the number and the street?
Oh, um. Honestly I'd rather not give the address on the phone. Is there a way to do it without? I can give you a callback number.
I do need to know where the street is for the crew to find it. Can you at least give me the name of the street and a cross street?
Hmm. Okay. I'm, uh, I'm sorry, I'm blanking, I'm a bit confused about what you need exactly. Can I just give you my number, and you call me, and I'll tell you then?

I can take your number and a note, sure. But I'll be honest, the request goes to the crew with the location, so someone would have to get the location from you either way. Let me take the number first. What's the best one?
It's four zero one, five five five, zero one five zero.
Four zero one, five five five, zero one five zero. And your name?
Vincent Fiore. F-I-O-R-E.

Thank you, Vincent, F-I-O-R-E. And the issue is a plow bank blocking the end of the driveway, plowed this morning, street itself is clear. Anything else the crew should know? Is anyone in the house needing to get out for something urgent?

Oh, no, no, nothing urgent. I mean, I do need to get the car out at some point. My neighbor actually offered to drive me where I need to go today, and I said no, thanks. I figured it'd be easier if it just got cleared and I could go myself.
Okay, so you have a ride available if you need it, but you'd rather get the car out yourself. I'll note that it's not an emergency but you'd like it cleared.
Right. Yes. That's it. Not an emergency.

Good. Now, generally, I can tell you the crews push the snow to the side of the road, and it does end up at the foot of driveways, I know that's no fun. Once the main roads are done they go back and do cleanup on the side streets as they can. I can't give you a time though.
Okay. That makes sense. So, like, today? Tomorrow? Just roughly.
I really can't say. It depends on what else is out there and how much came down. I'll put in the request and mark it as a plow returning to clear the end of your driveway.
Okay, cool. Wait, sorry, did you say the plow clears the driveway or the pile? Because, I mean, I thought the plow would just, um, I'm not sure how that works.

Good question. The plow can't really dig out your driveway. What it can do is, if the bank is sitting in the street or is a big windrow, a crew can come back and open it up. But the part right at your driveway opening is usually something the homeowner or resident shovels. So I'm putting in the request, but you may still have some shoveling to do.
Oh. Huh. Okay. So I might be shoveling anyway. [laughs] Sorry, I lost track, I thought I was getting a whole, like, a whole crew.

That's alright. A lot of people think that. So, let me read it back. Vincent Fiore, callback four zero one, five five five, zero one five zero. Plow left a heavy bank across the end of the driveway this morning, street is cleared, asking for a plow to come back. Not urgent. Did I get that right?
Yes. That's right. Except, um, the location. You said someone would call me for that?
If you'd like to give it to me now, I can attach it. Otherwise, whoever follows up will ask you for it when they call. It might take a bit.
Okay. I'll wait for the call, then. Thank you.
You're welcome, Vincent. Keep your phone nearby. Take care.
Thanks, Lorraine. Bye.
